players.product: optical fiber, fusion splicers & data-center interconnect components

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): net sales JPY 1,182.4 billion (+20.7% year on year), operating income JPY 188.7 billion (+39.2%), ordinary income JPY 199.5 billion (+45.4%), net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 157.2 billion (+72.5%). By segment: Information & Communications net sales JPY 653.0 billion (+44.7%) and operating income JPY 152.7 billion (+65.7%), as data-center demand driven by the spread and expansion of generative AI kept growing; Electronics net sales JPY 172.3 billion (-7.3%) and operating income down 66.5%, on a downstream supply-chain problem, intensifying competition and higher costs from the strong Thai baht; Automotive net sales JPY 179.4 billion (+1.3%) and operating income up 17.0%, as one-off inflation effects were passed into prices despite copper-price increases that could not be passed on in the period; Energy net sales JPY 157.0 billion (+8.1%) and operating income JPY 18.9 billion (+58.6%), on more shipments of high-margin products, better selling prices and derivative valuation gains from the copper-price rise; Real Estate net sales up 1.9%. No external customer accounted for 10% or more of consolidated net sales, so no major customer is disclosed.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 1,182.4 billion (+20.7%); operating income JPY 188.7 billion (+39.2%); Information & Communications sales JPY 653.0 billion (+44.7%), operating income JPY 152.7 billion (+65.7%)

quarterly_data.signal: 2028 Mid-Term Business Plan (published May 2026; annual securities report): for the plan's final year, fiscal 2028 (the year starting April 2028), the company targets net sales of JPY 1.6 trillion, operating income of JPY 315.0 billion, ROE of 28.5% and ROIC of 21.6%. The plan shifts from 'defensive' to 'offensive' selection and concentration, accelerating strategic investment in growth fields and concentrating resources on 'information infrastructure' and 'information storage', where data-center demand is expected to keep growing; it also pursues fusion energy. Management expects hyperscale data-center construction and data center interconnect (DCI) investment driven by generative AI to continue, keeping demand for optical wiring solutions at a high level, and expects hyperscale data-center demand centred on North America to keep expanding, with optical fiber cable and multi-fiber optical connector demand staying high; it will strengthen production capacity and supply. From fiscal 2026 (the year starting April 2026) the Electronics and Automotive segments are combined into a new Electronics & Electrical segment.
quarterly_data.figure: Fiscal 2028 (year starting April 2028) targets: net sales JPY 1.6 trillion; operating income JPY 315.0 billion; ROE 28.5%; ROIC 21.6%

quarterly_data.signal: Optical capacity expansion (annual securities report): in March 2026 the company decided to invest up to JPY 300.0 billion in total in Japan and the US to expand optical fiber cable production capacity up to 3 times the current level; under a framework agreement signed with the US Department of Commerce in October 2025, it aims to raise optical fiber and SWR/WTC capacity each to up to 3 times the current level. It invested to raise MT ferrule (a key part of multi-fiber optical connectors) capacity about 1.7 times versus fiscal 2024 (the year starting April 2024) and, with data-center demand still strong, is considering further expansion; it is also increasing MT/MMC ferrule output and strengthening wiring-component capacity at its Vietnam, Mexico and Poland plants. For optical cable, it is investing in WTC production equipment in Morocco, using the Automotive business's Moroccan plant, targeting operation in the first half of fiscal 2026 (April-September 2026), for a recovering European market and expansion in the Middle East and Africa.
quarterly_data.figure: Up to JPY 300.0 billion in Japan and the US; optical fiber cable capacity up to 3x; MT ferrule capacity about 1.7x vs fiscal 2024 (year starting April 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex and plant plans (annual securities report): capital expenditure in the year ended March 2026 totalled JPY 40.3 billion, concentrated on growth fields. At the Sakura Works (Sakura, Chiba) a next-generation optical fiber / SWR plant is under construction for about JPY 45.0 billion. Planned new facilities (Information & Communications): Sakura Works SWR new plant, total JPY 10,077 million (JPY 8,221 million already paid), started August 2023, completion June 2026, capacity increase 1.3 times; Sakura Works SWR new plant, total JPY 44,963 million (JPY 33 million paid), started August 2025, completion in fiscal 2029 (the year starting April 2029), capacity increase about 2 times.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 40.3 billion; Sakura SWR plant JPY 10,077 million (completion June 2026, 1.3x); Sakura SWR plant JPY 44,963 million (completion fiscal 2029 (year starting April 2029), about 2x)

quarterly_data.signal: Information & Communications products and R&D (annual securities report): in fiscal 2025 (the year ended March 2026) the company began selling what it calls the world's first 13,824-fiber SWR/WTC cable for hyperscale data centers, doubling the previous maximum of 6,912 fibers while keeping the outer diameter at 40 mm or less, and commercialised a 4,000-fiber SWR/WTC for the Japanese data-center market. It increased output of MMC (Miniature Multi-Row Connector) ferrules, which are being adopted in data centers, launched MMC trunk cables using SWR/WTC, and plans further increases in MMC ferrule and MMC trunk cable output. It developed a new multi-fiber fusion splicer, mainly for building generative-AI data centers, with sales planned from fiscal 2026 (the year starting April 2026) (automatic fiber alignment, end-gap correction, GPS logging), and a new core-alignment splicer for low-loss long-haul fiber. Segment R&D spending was JPY 11.5 billion of group R&D of JPY 16.8 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: 13,824-fiber WTC (vs 6,912 previous max), outer diameter 40 mm or less; segment R&D JPY 11.5 billion; group R&D JPY 16.8 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CPO and next-generation fiber (annual securities report): the company's polarization-maintaining fiber is increasingly being adopted for co-packaged optics (CPO), and its CPO shipments increased in fiscal 2025 (the year ended March 2026); it will focus on manufacturing technology to raise productivity and lower cost to meet growing demand. Next-generation optical fiber is a priority R&D area: multicore and hollow-core fiber for thinner diameter and lower loss, and applying PANDA fiber and image fiber technology to contribute to CPO and other opto-electronic integration. It has also developed composite modules integrating fiber couplers for submarine-cable repeaters.

Fusion and fiber lasers (annual securities report): high-temperature superconducting wire, used in the superconducting magnets of compact fusion reactors, is being expanded at the Sakura Works; the company decided in fiscal 2025 (the year ended March 2026) on a plant expansion of about JPY 5.6 billion and plans to raise capacity about 3-4 times versus fiscal 2024 (the year starting April 2024) in fiscal 2027 (the year starting April 2027) and about a further 2 times in fiscal 2028 (the year starting April 2028). Its single-mode fiber laser output was raised to 7 kW, it develops pulsed fiber lasers with semiconductor equipment makers for each process step, and it has partnerships with EX-Fusion and Blue Laser Fusion Inc. toward applying fiber lasers to laser fusion.
quarterly_data.figure: HTS wire plant expansion about JPY 5.6 billion; capacity about 3-4x vs fiscal 2024 in fiscal 2027, about 2x more in fiscal 2028 (Japanese fiscal years starting April); 7 kW single-mode fiber laser

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics outlook and data-center products (annual securities report): management expects smartphone demand at major customers, which use many FPCs and connectors, to stay firm, but is watching whether higher handset prices caused by surging memory prices hurt replacement demand; FPC will keep shifting to high-value-added products. For data centers it will strengthen HDD component production and thermal product development: new cold plates with a proprietary structure and higher-performance 3D vapor chambers for higher-heat CPUs/GPUs used in generative AI. Electronics R&D was JPY 2.4 billion. In Automotive, management expects global vehicle production to increase versus fiscal 2025 (the year ended March 2026), while watching US auto tariffs and the slowing EV market.
